utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, may we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, Your Honour, Kapila Waidyaratne, Mr. Nicholas Koumjian, and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before starting with today's witness, I have to announce the result of yesterday's, let's call it, attempt. First of all, I have here a memo from Peter Lawson, deputy commanding officer of the United Nations Detention Unit. It reads as follows: "Following a decision in the Trial Chamber this morning, a search of the cell of Mr. Stakic was carried out this afternoon by two United Nations Detention Unit officers, and in the presence of Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the President please speak in his microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The problem is that when I turn the microphone, we have the strange noise. Does it help now? Okay. I proceed: "In the presence of Mr. Stakic and me. Prior to the search, Mr. Stakic had identified all legal documents in his cell subject to attorney/client privilege. These documents were not searched. During the cell search, no documents were found which matched the description of the documents searched for. "After the search, all legal documents were put in boxes, four in total, sealed, and placed in a secure place outside of the cell of Mr. Stakic, for a Judge of the Tribunal to examine at a later stage." Following this, I have a memo from Judge Per Lindholm dated 23 July, 2002. It reads: "First, please be informed that on the evening of 22 July, 2002, I, along with my associate legal officer Katherine Gallagher, carried out a review of four boxes of documents belonging to the accused Milomir Stakic at the United Nations Detention Unit in order to identify and seize, if identified, originals of eight copied documents I had received from the Stakic Trial Chamber. "I received the boxes of documents from Peter Larsen, deputy commanding officer, and Hans Brauers [phoen], principal officer. All boxes were sealed with the signature of Stakic on each seal. "Four, the review of documents was carried in the premises of the United Nations Detention Unit with only myself and my ALO present. "Five, no originals of the copied documents were identified among the papers and documents contained in the four boxes belonging to Dr. Stakic. "Six, the four boxes with all their contents intact were returned to Dr. Stakic and his cell in my presence. I informed him that no documents had been removed from the boxes." Signed by Judge per Lindholm. Any observations by the parties as regards this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but I'm concerned. I would like the fact that there was a search done and no documents found to be part of the trial record. May we consider that -- may we have that report from the Detention Unit marked as an exhibit and admitted as part of the evidence in this case because I think it's relevant that, in fact, a search was done and none of the documents that had been returned to the accused were found in the cell. It has some evidentiary value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was the intention for the completeness of our documents to give these documents to the registry and have it as exhibits under "J." Are there any objections by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. We do not have an objection to the letter from the Judge being attached. However, we maintain our objection to have the provisional documents that were introduced by the Office of the Prosecution as a basis for their supplemental request for a subpoena. We would continue to maintain our objection to those documents being a part of the record, at least a formal record, for evidentiary purposes in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's fair enough. And having read the transcript of yesterday, I just want to confirm that indeed the document, for what purpose so ever, are admitted into evidence, those that were tendered yesterday by the OTP. I'm quite sure that in the future, they will form part of the one or other discussion. As regards the two other documents received just a minute ago, please let me know the next "J" number available is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be J9, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: J9. This is the document of Peter Larsen, and J10, the document provided by Judge Per Lindholm. May I ask the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we just ask for the completeness of our records that each of the parties gets a copy of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt. Any other observations before we start with today's witness? I can't see any. May the usher please bring in the witness. Thank you. It's my understanding that we continue in the beginning in private session. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But not closed session; private session is enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I ask whether your client has any complaints as regards the search yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we discussed with our client briefly those matters involving the search, and he does not have any complaints and has, as usual, been treated accordingly and appropriately. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I ask the OTP, objections as regards this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This was provided under 65 ter as document 319, if I am correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then these documents are admitted into evidence as D22 A, B respectively, and D23. The Defence may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness U, yesterday we discussed the Territorial Defence in Kozarac. And I'd like to ask you a question with respect to the negotiations and the meeting that you were involved with subsequent to the negotiations between the representatives of Kozarac and the representatives in Prijedor. With respect to that, sir, can you tell me whether or not at any time during that meeting there was a discussion in connection with forming a new municipality in the Kozara area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that meeting, the meeting I attended, only the result of the negotiations held by a certain group in Prijedor were discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it your testimony, sir, that there was not a discussion at any time regarding the formation of the Kozara Municipality in connection with the events that led to May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I contend that at the meeting I attended, there was no discussion of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you share with us, sir, if at any time prior to or subsequent to that meeting that you attended, was there ever a discussion by the Muslim citizens of the Kozarac area whether or not they were contemplating forming a separate municipality from the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was never into politics, as I've said already. The only thing I attended, I've already told you. But officially, I heard no such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this meeting, sir, yesterday, you shared with us the names of two individuals that spoke or of those which you recollect, namely, Dr. Jusuf Pasic and a Mr. Fazlic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified on page 14, line 10, yesterday that during this meeting the room was packed. Can you describe for us or give us the essence of how many people were present during the discussion at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number because I don't know. But I can describe the room perhaps. It's perhaps 6 by 7 metres, so between 35 and 40 square metres. And mainly, it was full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I know it was a long time ago, sir, but can you give us the best estimate as to how many people there were? Was it more or less than a hundred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be wrong if I said that it was more than a hundred perhaps. I can only say that the room was full and some people were seated and some people were standing. I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if the Madam Court Registrar would tender Exhibit Defence 17 A and B for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 7 A and B. Thank you. And for the purposes of the record, these were previously introduced into evidence which were summary meeting minutes from, we contend, citizens of the Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as you know, we are in open session, and so I'm going to ask you a couple questions in connection with the individuals who seem to be the same individuals who were present at the meeting in which you attended, namely, Mr. Fazlic and Dr. Pasic. Yesterday, sir, you described for us some of the comments that Dr. Pasic shared with you, and if you look on page 318 of that document, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make an observation here? There is no specific date given by this witness with regard to the meeting. And first, it may be appropriate if my -- the Defence counsel asked the witness whether it was on this specific date or more particulars with regard to this, as the witness may not be aware of -- this may be misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness U, can you tell us, in connection with the meeting in which you participated in or were present at which involved Dr. Pasic and Mr. Fazlic, can you tell us the time in which that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, I can't give you the date. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to remember if it was during the month of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe -- at any rate, I think it happened after the takeover of Prijedor Municipality by the Serbian Democratic Party. I believe it was immediately following that. Those may have been the first negotiations to follow the takeover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I suggest to you, sir, that the takeover, for purposes of our discussion here, was on or about April 30th, 1992, would it be fair to say, based on your recollection, that this meeting in which you participated in, in connection with the negotiations between the representatives of Kozarac and those of Prijedor, occurred sometime in early May 1992? Would that be a fair assumption on my part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an exact estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that based on some of the time lines that we've established in this case, namely, that the takeover occurred on or about April 30th, 1992, and the attack as you've described it yesterday, both during your direct examination and limited cross-examination, occurred on May 24th, 1992? Would it be a fair assumption on my part that the negotiations in which you were present at occurred in between the time period of April 30th, 1992, and May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Another observation, Your Honour. I don't know whether it was a mistake on the part of the Defence counsel. It says he never took part in the negotiations. This reads, as in the transcript, "Would it be a fair assumption on my part that the negotiations in which you were present at occurred..." There were no negotiations that he took part. It was a discussion and the results. The witness was very clear on that point, that these people came and spoke to them with regard to the negotiations and the results as to what took part in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may restate the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness U, in connection with your presence which followed the negotiations by the leaders or representatives of the Kozarac area between the Kozarac area representatives and those of Prijedor representatives, you participated in a meeting in which the representatives of Kozarac informed you of the results of one meeting in which they participated in. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with that, sir, understanding that you were not one of the negotiators at those meetings between the Kozarac representatives and the Prijedor representatives, is it true that the meeting in which you participated in occurred in between April 30th, 1992, and May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't say. I can't confirm this if I just simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can confirm it in a different fashion, sir. Do you recall if, in fact, the meeting that you took place occurred after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the attack on Kozarac, I had been in the camp for two or three days already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it logical or may I assume, sir, that in fact this meeting in which you participated or took place in or were present at, occurred sometime prior to May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, prior to that. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting, sir, do you remember whether or not Dr. Pasic discussed any issue in connection with insignia that the Bosnian Muslims were preparing to create and put on the individual police officers and Territorial Defence members for that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. At the meeting, I did not hear any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, yesterday during your direct examination, you shared with us that Dr. Pasic, in essence, said, and please correct me if I am wrong, "We are occupied. The aggressor imposes its authority on us. We can either accept it until some better times, or get in to war."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the purposes of the transcript, please, where did you quote from? What page?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quite frankly, Your Honour, it's a summary. It's not from the transcript. It's specifically from page 318 of Exhibit D7A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that, sir, the sum and substance of the recollection you have of Dr. Pasic's statements that you shared with us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you the essence yesterday, and I can repeat it for you today and you can cull from it whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Perhaps to be more specific, on page 14 of your transcript yesterday, line 7 through 20, you identify Dr. Pasic. And specifically at page 10 and 11, you state as follows: "So, Jusuf Pasic perhaps simplified the matter a bit, and this is literally what he said. He said: 'As negotiators,' and I am referring to the group who had gone to Prijedor to negotiate, `we are in an unequal position as a negotiating team to negotiate our terms, and you must be aware of that.' He was referring to us who were listening, `they,' and I am here referring to the Prijedor municipal authorities, `are the occupation force.' That's what he said." You proceed to tell us: "And they tell us what to do. And they are not asking us what we thought was done. They are not requesting our proposals. This is something you must understand. That's what the situation is like," he said. Ending on page 14, line 20. Is that, sir, what your testimony was as to your recollection of what Dr. Pasic said at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that during that meeting, someone specifically took minutes of the various speakers that were present at that meeting, including Dr. Pasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean that particular meeting that I attended?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we're discussing only that particular meeting in which you were present, correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't notice anyone taking any sort of minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, during that meeting at any time whether or not there was a discussion of the provocation by the Muslim citizens of Prijedor against the Serbs and the Serb military in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You wanted to say "a provocation," and not "the provocation." Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that meeting, other relations were not discussed. And I'm only referring to the meeting where the negotiations were held, and that was the only thing I heard. Maybe other stories were told there but this is the only thing I still recollect. And probably the meeting was longer and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. probably contained more than what I have been able so far to recollect and recount for you here. But if anyone was taking minutes, perhaps you can produce that. I don't myself remember any further details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, if I may, sir, with respect to that meeting, refresh your recollection or probe, and I understand that you don't recall a discussion regarding the insignia or a provocation. Do you recall, sir, a discussion specifically by Dr. Pasic where during the time he stated that "The aggressor imposes its authority on us," he proceeds to tell the people who were present during this meeting: "They claim that the army will not interfere." Do you recall specifically Dr. Pasic ever informing the citizens during that meeting of the result of the negotiations between the Prijedor representatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear any such thing. I would like to add something, if I can. This list does not include the people who were present at that meeting. It is not that delegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to identify, in addition to Mr. Fazlic and Dr. Pasic, who were present at the delegation of negotiators, who else in connection with the meeting that you were present at was the so-called delegation that met with the representatives in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The surname "Fazlic" is correct, but not the first name. On the other hand, I don't see the surname "Pasic" here anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would be kind enough, sir, on your Exhibit D7, which is the B/C/S version of the document, on page -- on the top right-hand corner, 339, if you can turn to that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And for the Court, it appears on page 318 of D7A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and -- do you have a copy for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do not, Your Honour. It's an exhibit, so I assumed obviously incorrectly, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Apparently it causes some difficulties, and maybe we are discussing different meetings. And as far as the witness has stated until now, he can't recognise the meeting you are referring to as the meeting he has participated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I understand that. And that is the purpose for which I asked the following question, so that he can read to himself the full context of the statement that's attributed to Pasic in connection with that. And based on his testimony yesterday on direct examination - although perhaps somewhat argumentative - it seems to be parallel and, therefore, we're making the assumption that that was the same meeting, although there were quite a number of other meetings within a group Exhibit 7 A and B which were recorded. So perhaps if the witness, with the Court's permission, is given one last opportunity to review that short paragraph, then he can tell us whether or not that was the meeting in which he was present. And I'm prepared to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As you correctly stated, it's an assumption only, and finalise this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness U, would you be kind enough to review the paragraph and section on page 338 that's before you, which are the comments and statements attributed to Dr. Pasic. 339, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the only thing I can see here is words. I mean, there are just several words that I can read here. The rest is illegible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. If I may move on, but still on this same line of questioning, sir, do you know how many meetings subsequent to the one that you participated in or knew about were held between the representatives of the Kozarac area and those of the Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. The witness can't answer this question because evidently he was not present in all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of any meetings between the representatives of the Kozarac area and those of the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already mentioned this piece of information after the meeting that I attended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Are you aware, sir, of any meetings that occurred between those representative groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you state on page 14 of your transcript yesterday, in connection with this meeting, line 23: "But probably the result of those negotiations was precisely the attack of the Serb force on the 24th and 25th of May, 1992." In connection with this statement, sir, are you aware of the fact that there was an announcement made on or about May 22nd, 1992, by the federal and/or Republic Yugoslav military that requested that the Muslim citizens and the checkpoints that existed on the main Prijedor/Banja Luka Road were to be removed 100 metres from the road so that the military convoy can pass safely and securely through both Kozarac and Prijedor? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, nor do I know that there were checkpoints in these locations. I believe I said yesterday that the checkpoints were 100 to 200 metres away from the main road. Where they were on the 23rd, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that on or about May 24th, prior to the attack by the military in the Kozarac area, the military were ambushed and actually sustained casualties and injuries, the very first truck of that convoy, as it was passing through the area of Jakupovici through the Prijedor/Banja Luka main road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such thing. I've never heard of that until now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that two days prior to this attack on Kozarac, in an area called Hambarine, on May 22nd, 1992, there was an attack by Muslims against a Serb military officer passing through a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What happened there, I didn't know. Two or three nights prior to the attack on Kozarac, I had heard artillery fire in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To this day, sir, and I understand that it has been ten years approximately and more since the date of that May 22nd, 1992, incident, can you tell us if you are aware of any incidents of provocation by the Muslims against the Serbs following the takeover of Prijedor on or about April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a general question. He is asking for opinion from the witness. He is asking to generalise things, not a specific question put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. Probably the question may be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware, in May of 1992, a Serb police officer was killed in the town of Prijedor, in the municipality of Prijedor, immediately after the takeover of Prijedor Municipality by the Serbs? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you likewise, sir, unaware that on May 30th, 1992, there was a group of paramilitary or Muslim forces that attacked the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't comment or answer that question. I simply was not able to know everything, what kind of paramilitary groups there were. All I can say is I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the paramilitary group called Ramiz's group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I think following the line of questions, the witness clearly has indicated that he is not familiar with what happened in the surroundings. And I think it even doesn't assist the Chamber when you proceed with this line of questions. We have covered this already in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it fair to state as you've stated previously in your statement of March 13th and 14th, 2000, that you did not hear any particular propaganda programme on the radio or TV during the period of April through August 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could counsel be so kind and quote the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, page 2 of the witness statement of March 13th, 14th 2000, specifically paragraph number 4, which is a one-line paragraph on Bate stamp 00935047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, with the Court's permission, just restate the question for the witness. I'm not sure if I received an oral response, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness U, is it fair to state that you "did not hear any particular propaganda programme on radio or TV" during the period of April through August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't think the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I did not listen to such programmes. I may have heard them, but I didn't pay much attention to that. I didn't consider those programmes to be interesting for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question on this, sir, and I can appreciate that. Is it fair to say that you have no recollection as to who the speakers may have been at that time or the contents of the material which was provided on those programmes? Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, prior to April of 1992, did Serb soldiers return from Croatia and pass through the municipality of Prijedor? Do you remember that event happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if these were soldiers who were under the auspices of the federal government, the republic government, or any other entity that you may be aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Convoys were passing, and according to what I knew, they were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, if I may, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I direct your attention to your statement of May 13th, 14th, 2000, and I will quote it because unfortunately I do not have a copy for you. But bear with me on this. It's on paragraph 5 of page 2 of that statement, as follows: "When Serb soldiers were returning from Croatia, they passed through our villages, and they shot all around. It was common knowledge that Serbs armed themselves." Is it your testimony, sir, now that these Serb soldiers that you're referencing actually came from Serbia or Croatia, or was your answer, in fact, that the Serb soldiers that you reference were part of the federal government of the Former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, I think that the Yugoslav People's Army still existed. I am not familiar with the various formations of the army at the top. As for the people that I spoke about, those who passed through our village in convoy, both ways, coming and going, they did shoot from their trucks and other vehicles as they were passing through our villages. That is correct. As for this second sentence, the last one that you mentioned, that it was common knowledge that Serbs armed themselves, it's actually -- it was actually my knowledge. I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll take one at a time, if I may. Is it not true, sir, that when you state the Serb soldiers who were shooting were actually shooting in the air and did not shoot at individual citizens in the area of the Prijedor Municipality, including the village in which you resided at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that they were shooting at citizens. I said that they were shooting in the air as they were passing through our villages. Had they shot at us, they would have killed us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, with respect to the second comment or issue that we were dealing with, it being your personal common knowledge of the Serbs arming themselves, can you please explain to me how you became aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there are several versions as to how I came to know that. As an example, having passed through the town of Kasnice in the vicinity of Banja Luka, on the Banja Luka/Prnjavor Road, I came across a -- I had to stop on the bridge. There were several other vehicles ahead of me. There was a convoy of soldiers passing by coming from the direction of Bihac, members of the air force, which I presumed were leaving the area at the time. It's also possible that these soldiers were going on leave. I'm not sure. But anyway, this convoy was stopped by a military vehicle. It was actually a military police vehicle, olive-grey in colour. I don't know what the purpose of this stopping was, but an argument ensued. And after about two hours, because we were also ordered to stop and form a blockade on the road while they were arguing and discussing, so at that moment, I saw that all civilians, all men, had come out and that they were all armed. Every one of them had a weapon. I don't know how many of them there were at the time. But I realised that the local people, local individuals there, were armed. They all had weapons at their homes. I could see that for myself, and this is what I based my statement on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, are you aware at any time prior to your detention on May 26th, 1992, at the Trnopolje camp, at any time prior to that, sir, whether or not the Muslim population, whether it was within your village or any other villages you may have some common knowledge of, whether they were also armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is probable that they were armed, but then one would expect that I would be armed. I don't know why they would leave me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, sir, you stated yesterday on page 16 of your direct examination, line 15, in describing the attack on Kozarac and the Kozara area, that you saw for yourself, "a shell land on a roof, and the house just fell apart, and the roof started burning." Specifically for the record, line 15 through 16, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your albeit limited military experience, having been in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the reserves or having served, do you know what effect a grenade would have if it would implode on a home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My knowledge about the effect of grenades and similar detonations is rather modest. I merely told you about what I had seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the shell that you saw that hit the roof of a house and subsequently destroying the house, causing the roof to burn, do you know what that shell was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true, sir, that in fact you witnessed and saw grenades hit houses, plural as opposed to singular, as you testified to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grenades hitting houses, I don't know. I said that when the shells started to fall, I did not actually see them. I just felt pieces of houses, rubble of the surrounding houses, falling all around me. I took shelter in the garage. And because there was no door at the front, I could not directly see all of these houses. I could only indirectly see one of them. And when the shell hit this house, everything started falling around. And after that, I saw the blaze.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that during the time in which you drove this wounded individual to the hospital in Kozarac, that in fact you saw plural grenades hit plural houses? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I think the witness has clearly answered first the question as regards the one house he saw, and then on your -- on the basis of your leading questions, he answered the question as regards to similar and other houses. I think the question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Witness U, if you can reconcile this for me. In your statement on March 13th, 14th, 2000, specifically paragraph 8, which is the second-to-the-last paragraph, on page 2 of your statement, in the middle of the statement, you state: "During the driving, I could see that grenades hit houses."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the driving, I said that I was holding this man. The truck was covered with canvas. And during the ride, the canvas flapped and billowed as a result of the wind. And throughout that ride, I was not able to see all of the houses. But at those moments when the canvas was lifted, I could see that some of the houses had been hit. I couldn't observe everything. I didn't see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you identify with respect to this hospital in which you took this wounded man, can you give me the name of that hospital in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the name. I don't know whether it had a name. We simply called it a hospital, although it did not admit bedridden patients. It was just a medical centre. But we called it the hospital. It was probably a department of the central hospital in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I recognise, sir, you do not remember the name of the hospital. But do you remember, sir, if this facility in which you brought this wounded man was actually created and set up immediately after April 30th, 1992, by the citizens of the Kozara area, and that it was only a temporary facility in anticipation of perhaps some sort of confrontation or battle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The facility had been functioning for years already. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one last question, if I may, with respect to the shelling that you saw during the May 24th through 26th, 1992, period. On page 20, sir, of your testimony yesterday, line 15 specifically, you state, just so that you may have it in context: "Ever since the very beginning of the shelling and my departure from that area, rounds kept falling almost all the time, but sporadically, with intervals." Ending on line 17 of page 20 of your transcript. Can you with any more precision, sir, explain or describe for me what you mean by both the words "sporadically, with intervals"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I can be more precise as to the intervals. The breaks, the lulls, probably lasted half an hour, maybe one hour. There's nothing more I can tell you about these intervals. It's just that one couldn't hear the shooting all the time. It was sporadic. But it lasted from the 24th until the 26th of May, at intervals, sporadically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of any resistance by the citizens of that area against the military convoy that was passing through on or about May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any convoy passing through at that time, although I stayed very close to the road. I don't know where they could have possibly have passed without me seeing them. So I didn't see any such convoy. Whether anyone was putting up resistance, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to state, sir, that the sporadic shooting or shelling that you heard, you are unaware from whom that sporadic shooting was being started by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the shooting. I don't know. I only know that at 2.00 on the 24th, shells started falling from heavy artillery weapons, which means that it wasn't infantry weapons being used, which I was familiar with from my days in the military, unlike with the artillery weapons. And this is all I can say. But how it all started and who was involved, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple questions briefly on a different issue, sir. Are you aware prior to April 30th, 1992, of an influx of Serbian refugees from Croatia in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I've never heard anything about this so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that during the period prior to April 30th, 1992, that the Muslim citizens, some Muslim citizens in the Prijedor Municipality, actually left the area or left the municipality in light of the tension and atmosphere that was being created both politically and militarily in the region of the republic or the former Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know of any such citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, since my question prior to that was for the period prior to April 30th, 1992, are you aware that subsequent to April 30th, 1992, whether there was ever a convoy of Muslim citizens who decided to leave the Prijedor Municipality voluntarily and on their own?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object to that question, Your Honour. Earlier it was prior to the 30th of April, but there have been many convoys after that. Your Honours have heard many witnesses talking about people leaving: Muslims, non-Serbs leaving Prijedor area. So if my learned friend could restrict or say a specific time period, that would be much appropriate. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. Probably you may rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, from the period of April 30th, 1992 through May 26th, 1992, approximately the time in which you were detained in the Trnopolje Detention Centre, were you, sir, aware of any Muslims voluntarily leaving the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While I was still detained, the 26th of May, you said? I'm sorry, I didn't quite follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend from the Office of the Prosecutor wished me to put a time limitation, so the period in which I'm interested to know if you obtained any information or knowledge is specifically from the period of April 30th, 1992, up until, but not after, May 26th, which is the date, as you've testified, sir, yesterday, the date in which you were incarcerated and placed in the Trnopolje Detention Centre. For that limited 25 days, are you aware or do you have any information, sir, in connection with Muslims in the Prijedor Municipality, including the villages in which you were at, whether or not they were voluntarily leaving the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my village where I lived, in that period, I didn't notice anyone leaving. And I think everyone was in their homes when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, sir, what date you attribute to the "war breaking out"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 24th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may now, sir, turn to the time period that you spent in the Trnopolje camp. And just so that we're talking about specifically the right time frame, you testified yesterday that from May 26th, 1992, through October 1st, 1992, you were detained in the Trnopolje Detention Centre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were there, sir, specifically on May 26th, 1992, can you tell us whether or not there were barbed wires that surrounded the entire Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The entire duration of my stay there, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you initially, during your incarceration on May 26th, 1992, was there a barbed wire fence at the Trnopolje camp that surrounded the Trnopolje Detention Centre or school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Barbed wire fence, there never was one around the school building. They put one up outside the cinema building, that is, actually behind the cinema building, the cultural centre, and around it for a while. But not on the first day. No, it wasn't there on the first day as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir. When you say, "They put one up around the cinema building, or behind the cinema building, the cultural centre," who is the "they" that you are referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am referring to persons who probably - actually certainly - following orders by someone from the military, took up -- by orders from the camp command or some other command, they brought the barbed wire over there and put it up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me, sir, if you would be kind enough to tell me what period of time this occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't specify the period of time. That was not right at the very beginning; it may have been -- please, don't take this too literally, but I think probably after a month. I really don't know. I couldn't specify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when, according to you, sir, were these barbed wires removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know when they were removed. The front side, I think it remained. I think so, but I can't say with certainty. The lower side, there's an open field leading to a football pitch. For a day or two, they placed there a sort of a metal net, netting, and posts were driven into the ground. And this lasted for a day or two, I think. And then the same people came back. Probably, they had orders by someone who had brought them there. They just pulled this net down to the ground, and that's how it then remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, sir, during the period in which you were at the Trnopolje Detention Centre, from May 26th, 1992, through October 1st, 1992, that the population within that Detention Centre was both mixed in age and gender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds fair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's fair to say that there were women at the camp, sir, as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, temporarily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How temporarily were they there, sir? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they were expelled from their homes, from the surrounding villages, they would drive them as far as the cinema building or the school building, or wherever there was room to put them up. And sometimes they would stay there for two or three, sometimes even seven days, up to the day of their transport by rail in a direction I did not know at the time. I could not tell where these people were being taken off to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to state, sir, that from May 26th, 1992 all the way through August 15th, 1992, the Trnopolje Detention Centre actually had within its facilities both men and women at all times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question was already answered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us for the period of time that you were at Trnopolje camp whether or not there were any German shepherds that were purportedly manning the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see them. But I did see soldiers, individuals, with such dogs who would enter the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, with respect to the Trnopolje Detention Centre, whether or not there were any land mines in the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't check.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With -- pardon me? You may finish. I'm not sure if you finished your answer, sir. I interrupted you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Land mines, how am I supposed to know? I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, during the period in which you were detained at the Trnopolje Detention Centre, do you recall having gone across the street to obtain water for yourself, and perhaps for others, within the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in order for you and others to obtain this water, that you actually had to leave the Trnopolje facility as it was identified by you yesterday, both with the school, the cinema, and the cultural centre? Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we drew a line, where the line was passing what was the camp and what was outside the camp, I couldn't determine really because even in front and behind the guard posts, so anywhere within the range of the weapons the guards were carrying was camp for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Court -- I have a couple of other questions on the camp itself but it may be a convenient time, or if the Court wishes, I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The time is appropriate for having a break, but the Trial Chamber has decided to impose a time limit of only further 30 minutes. The trial stays adjourned until 15 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. U, with respect to the Trnopolje camp, before the break, we were specifically discussing water. I'd like to now turn to the topic of food. Is it fair, sir, and correct, to state that in fact food was provided to the detainees in the Trnopolje camp from the beginning of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your stay throughout the period of time in which you were at the Trnopolje Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not provided food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that in fact the Red Cross provided the detainees within the Trnopolje Detention Centre bread on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during the first days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that during the time in which you were at the Trnopolje Detention Centre, namely, May 26th through October 1st, 1992, that there were people, specifically women, who were permitted and allowed to go outside the camp and bring food for the people who were in the camp during the period of time in which you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women who went out to fetch food for the people in the camp, later those women were from the surrounding villages. They had not been expelled from their homes. And because they were in a position to, they brought food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Describe for me, if you will, how often these women in the surrounding areas would come into the Trnopolje Detention Centre and provide food for the people within the Trnopolje Detention Centre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Firstly, this was not an organised thing. They did it of their own free will. Whoever had food brought some to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, if they had any relatives and whatever they had to bring from their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this, sir, also happen after the purported barbed wire was placed on or around the area of the Trnopolje Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't specify the date when the last village in the surroundings of the camp was evacuated and, therefore, I can't give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me an approximate date, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This lasted until, perhaps, the first days, the early days, of August. I think, up to that point, there had been large convoys taking the women and children away. So in the course of August, this aspect of assistance ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, the type of food that you yourself received from May 26th until the beginning of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first days, as I've mentioned, the food we received consisted of slices of bread, two slices each. We would queue up, and we each got two slices of bread within 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequent to that, sir, with respect specifically to the women who were bringing the food to the camp, do you remember what type of food they were bringing into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They mainly brought whatever they had. Personally, I did not receive food from anyone myself, as an individual. But colleagues who were there with me had relatives who brought them food, so I shared some of their food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, how, if you know, were these women allowed to gain access to the Detention Centre if there was a barbed wire that surrounded the camp, to come on whatever basis it is that you recall they came into the Detention Centre to provide for the members within that Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber has been tolerant enough during the last hour on this question, and it was quite clearly stated and there is no remaining doubt. So I would ask you to stop this line of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I do have one more question, with respect. It doesn't include, Your Honour, if the Court permits, with the food issue, as the witness testified specifically on page 53 subsequent to the women in August being, as he put it, removed from the camp, how the detainees within the Trnopolje Detention Centre were able to have access to food. If I may just inquire on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One single question, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday during your direct examination on page 53, specifically, line 7 through 8 of your testimony, you stated that after these women no longer provided food to the Detention Centre, that, in fact, on line 8: "They would allow us to go and forage for food in the surrounding areas." Again, line 8, page 53 of yesterday's transcript. Can you tell me, sir, how often and what type of food would you bring back to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Allowed us, this doesn't mean that we could all go out within the time span of one day and then all come back within the span of one day. This was an individual thing and was only on account of the goodwill of the guards who were there and who allowed individuals to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple more questions, if I may, sir, with respect to the Trnopolje camp, unrelated to food, of course. With respect to any beatings at the camp, is it fair to say, sir, that you did not personally see any beatings at the Trnopolje camp during the time in which you were there, namely, May 26th through October 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see with my own eyes that anyone was beaten up inside the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also, sir, true that you did not at any time during the time in which you were at the Trnopolje Detention Centre from May 26th through October 1st, 1992, that you, sir, did not witness any killings in the camp whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not witness any such thing personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, sir, with respect to the women that were at the camp, I note on page 53 of yesterday's direct examination, specifically, line 22, you state: "As far as harassment of women is concerned, during my stay, I did not notice any such cases." Specifically, lines 22 through 23 of page 53. My question -- and then you proceed, sir, in all fairness to give us something that I think you either heard or were aware of. But my question to you, sir: Is it fair to state that you also did not see either males or females being harassed at the Trnopolje camp during the stay -- during your stay there, from May 26th through October 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I said I did not see, that meant I did not personally witness any such acts. I only personally saw the consequences of such acts, or I heard about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, is it also true that the camp commander as you've identified him to be a Major Slobodan Kuruzovic, correct, of the Trnopolje Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how often you would see Mr. Kuruzovic or Major Kuruzovic in the camp during the period in which you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if you would ever see Major Kuruzovic at the camp in the evenings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not too often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you described a situation in which you overheard Major Kuruzovic state, once he was confronted by the female detainees at the Trnopolje Detention Centre in connection with an incident that occurred perhaps a night or two prior relating to rapes or assaults on women, that Major Kuruzovic, in fact, stated that "This must not happen again." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may turn to another issue, sir, in the limited time that we have. Are you aware at any time during the period at issue, namely, April 1992 through September 1992, whether or not there was a Crisis Staff in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Between April 1992 and September 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, it's not on the transcript -- oh, here it comes. Thank you. Just so that I'm clear, and I apologise for having to perhaps re-ask the question, was this Crisis Staff in Kozarac, would you know who the members of this Crisis Staff were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say there was any such Crisis Staff in that period. As to who the members were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to April of 1992, do you know or are you familiar with any of the residents or citizens of the Kozarac area forming a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may just have been an error on line 17 of page 40 of today's transcript wherein it was given that you answered in the affirmative, but thank you for clarifying that. In connection, lastly, with respect to Crisis Staff, are you familiar, sir, at any time whether or not there was a Crisis Staff that was formed in the Kamicani area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only say that if there had been a Crisis Staff in the Kozarac area, probably the municipal -- the local commune authorities could have done that. But I cannot say whether they had, in fact, set up any such bodies and whether those bodies were in function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Briefly, right before your arrest and detention into Trnopolje camp, you stated that you took your truck and went towards the area of the woods opposite in which your family were going towards Trnopolje, so you were going in the opposite direction. And I believe that you said that there was a group of you. Can you tell me the number of people who were with you, who were going in the direction of the woods, on or before May 26th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I did not go on a tractor, and second, probably all of the population who happened to be at the bottom of the hill went in the direction of the woods to seek shelter there. My family was not that close, I mean, they had already gone in the opposite direction, and that is the reason why I subsequently decided to join them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. So how many people were there that went in the direction of the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that everybody left, but people were not in a group. So it was not possible for me to see them as a group going towards the woods. But my assumption is that all of the residents who were in the area, in view of the fact that the woods were very close, went there to seek shelter. At least, that was my idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if any of the people who were going towards the woods that you may have seen, whether or not any of them were armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you a moment ago that I had not seen a group of people going there. I couldn't see that, at least, people moving in a group. I wanted to go there because it was some kind of natural shelter because of the nature of the terrain, and it is only my assumption that all of my neighbours had also set out in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness U.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be permitted to ask two questions in private session which directly relate to some of the testimony that was elicited by my learned friends at the Office of the Prosecutor yesterday, also in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any questions in re-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: One question, Your Honour, in which to clarify a certain point which transpired during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Witness, when you were in the Trnopolje camp, you were clear enough and said that you didn't see any beatings, beating of prisoners or detainees who were in the Trnopolje camp. But did you see those people who were in the Trnopolje camp, the prisoners or the detainees, with injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. I didn't see it with my own eyes but I could see the consequences of the beatings on these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you explain as to how and when these people sustained the injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they would show up with a list. Sometimes they would just call out names and surnames and take detainees to the building of a catering facility which was right across the street from the building where the commander was, where the commander was staying. And according to my knowledge, that is where they were beaten up and mistreated. And it was from there that they returned wounded and injured. And I was able to see them when they came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: When you were at the Trnopolje camp, were you beaten or harassed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I can say that I was beaten, but they did hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just add one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Earlier this afternoon, you told us that indeed you were never interested especially in politics. But tell me one thing: With a view to the map Kamicani, the area you lived in, it seems to be relatively far away from Prijedor. Did you, before being arrested the 26th of May, 1992, ever hear the name of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear and precise answer. Judge Fassi Fihri, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you helped in the burial of nine persons that you had found in this basement you told us about. Were there any women amongst these nine individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eight people, and there were women amongst them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me think. Three. Three women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have another question for you, Witness: While you were in Trnopolje, did anyone die? Were there any deaths during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A lot, many? How many? Do you know? Do you have an idea of the number of such cases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I indicated one such case, the one that I eyewitnessed. People died during my stay there but I don't know the causes of their deaths, whether this was as a result of an illness or something else. There were cases that I know about, that I knew about, people whose bodies were carried out to a nearby cemetery, where they were eventually buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who transported these bodies, detainees, people like you, or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think it was with the assistance of the guards. But I don't think that it could have been done without the assistance of the guards, but it was actually done by the detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were there many such cases, fatal cases, these dead people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, not many people died inside the camp itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Vassylenko. No further questions. Any questions emanating from the questions of the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This then concludes the testimony of Witness U. Witness U, I have to thank you very much for not only coming here, but also to go through this line of important questions and answering really with a huge amount of tolerance. And we all know it's very difficult for you to go through these questions, sometimes from your point of view, indeed, difficult to understand. But believe us, you really assisted us in coming closer to the truth and we are extremely grateful for this. Thank you for that. The witness may be brought out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the OTP, the next witness should be number 42, the witness is available immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What kind of protection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No protective measures. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could the usher before in the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I be permitted to address Your Honour? Your Honour, there was a document which I said I would indicate whether we have a full translation of that document. I have been informed that we have not a full translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This was Document D22.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we proceed with the testimony of Witness 42. The estimated time of the examination-in-chief will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would estimate about three hours, two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have the proofing notes. The Defence also has the proofing notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any additional exhibits to be expected?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. I just anticipate using one of the maps that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the witness, no protection, we can use the name. Witness Mr. Poljak may be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the usher can already open the blinds when we have heard the solemn declaration. Mr. Poljak, good afternoon. You can understand me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please hear your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, sit down. And in the meantime, we can start the examination-in-chief. And may I ask the usher to open the blinds because we don't need any kind of protective measures in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Koumjian, please start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, would you please tell the Court your name?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: My name is Samir Poljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Poljak, when were you born?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I was born on the 1st of April, 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Jakupovici, which is part of the Kevljani local commune and the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Which is the bigger unit? Is Kevljani part of Jakupovici, or is -- which is bigger?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: That's a good question. We belong to the Kevljani local commune, but I think that Jakupovici is actually larger than Kevljani because it consists of three hamlets, Gornja Jakupovici, Srednji Jakupovici, and Donja Jakupovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Poljak, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I became a (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I just ask that the citizenship be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please redact the citizenship on the previous line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In 1992, did you -- were you a Muslim and considered yourself a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In 1992 - you said you were born in 1973 - were you 19 years old then, from April 30th of 1992, and May and thereafter in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I was 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What were you doing in the spring of 1992 before the conflict broke out? Did you work or go to school?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I attended secondary school. I was about to complete the fourth form of the secondary school. My school was technical school in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was it in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sometime that spring, did you stop going to classes, and if so, can you explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: When Serb authorities took over the municipality, I stopped going to school as of that day because my parents thought that it was better for me not to continue going to school for my own safety, to have a break and then to continue when the time comes. So I stopped going to school at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Prior to the armed conflict breaking out in 1992 in Prijedor, had you had any military training? Had you served in the Yugoslav army or the TO?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: No. I had not served in the JNA. I had not completed any kind of military service or training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you live at home in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I lived with my parents at our family house throughout that period of time, up until the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What was your father's name?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: Zihad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What was your father's occupation?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: He worked for the forestry most of his life, cutting wood, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did anyone else live in your house at that time besides you and your parents?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: My brother and his wife, with their son, who at the time was six months old.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you recall the events that happened on the 24th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Tell us in your own words what you remember about that day.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: That day, the situation was really tense, should I say the whole day, since early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: First, let me ask you: Where were you that day, let's say up until noon that day?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And starting from the pertinent events that happened that day from the morning, from noon on, tell us what you recall about what happened.

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I remember clearly, around 1.00 in the afternoon, I was sitting in my house, I was having lunch. On the table, we had a radio set, tape recorder. How should I say that? I was listening to Radio Prijedor. At that time, they had news on the radio, and they carried a piece of news which really scared me in a way. They said that unless the barricades were removed from the Banja Luka/Prijedor main road, Kozarac and the surrounding area would be attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have the map put on the ELMO that is Exhibit S51, 5-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Poljak, looking at this map, is it correct that this shows the area of Kozarac from the right of the eastern, southeastern side, Omarska, through Kozarac and Kozarusa, and then up north to the Kozara mountain area and the Benkovac area? Do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: Yes, Kozarac, Omarska, the Banja Luka/Prijedor main road. The old road, I recognise the old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you point on the map to where the village or area that your house was at in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: I think it was here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you actually live in Kevljani?

utterances.speaker: SAMIR POLJAK
utterances.text: No.
